newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr dragged to soft close by Australian unit.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr dragged to soft close by Australian unit.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar coasted to a lower close on Thursday after a quiet trading session, but dealers said the kiwi was basically paralysed in a US$0.6860-10 range ahead of key data next week.
The kiwi ended at 0.6875/80, against its 0.6887/94 open and 0.6892/99 finish on Wednesday. On its Trade-Weighted Index, the kiwi was at 67.54, from 67.68 at the open.
"The market has traded with a slightly weaker bias, just on the back of the Aussie. Flows today have been pretty light," one dealer said.
By 6.00 p.m. NZ time the Australian dollar was at US$0.7480/85, against Wednesday's late 0.7515/20.

Dealers said there was still the possibility of more eurokiwi issuance to give the kiwi a small fillip, but the market appeared quite comfortable to hold its current positions and a eurokiwi would not be sufficient to bunt it out of its range.

One dealer said he expected US$0.6910 to cap the currency ahead of next week's budget (Thursday) and RBNZ monetary policy statement (Friday), and that the kiwi would quietly trade lower in the interim.
